title: Aggregated External AI & Tech News
description: Merged headlines from configured external sources

items.title: Trump gets data center companies to pledge to pay for power generation (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: With no enforcement and questionable economics, it may not make a difference.

items.title: Downdetector, Speedtest sold to IT service-provider Accenture in $1.2B deal (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Accenture plans to buy Ookla, which also includes RootMetrics and Ekahau.

items.title: LLMs can unmask pseudonymous users at scale with surprising accuracy (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Pseudonymity has never been perfect for preserving privacy. Soon it may be pointless.

items.title: Google quantum-proofs HTTPS by squeezing 15kB of data into 700-byte space (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Merkle Tree Certificate support is already in Chrome. Soon, it will be everywhere.

items.title: New AirSnitch attack bypasses Wi-Fi encryption in homes, offices, and enterprises (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: That guest network you set up for your neighbors may not be as secure as you think.

items.title: Password managers' promise that they can't see your vaults isn't always true (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Contrary to what password managers say, a server compromise can mean game over.

items.title: Most VMware users still "actively reducing their VMware footprint," survey finds (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Broadcom's "strategy was never to keep every customer," CloudBolt report says.

items.title: Retraction: After a routine code rejection, an AI agent published a hit piece on someone by name (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: This story has been retracted

items.title: OpenAI sidesteps Nvidia with unusually fast coding model on plate-sized chips (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: OpenAI's new GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark is 15 times faster at coding than its predecessor.

items.title: Attackers prompted Gemini over 100,000 times while trying to clone it, Google says (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Distillation technique lets copycats mimic Gemini at a fraction of the development cost.

items.title: Once-hobbled Lumma Stealer is back with lures that are hard to resist (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: ClickFix bait, combined with advanced Castleloader malware, is installing Lumma "at scale."

items.title: OpenAI researcher quits over ChatGPT ads, warns of "Facebook" path (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Zoë Hitzig resigned on the same day OpenAI began testing ads in its chatbot.

items.title: Sixteen Claude AI agents working together created a new C compiler (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: The $20,000 experiment compiled a Linux kernel but needed deep human management.

items.title: Malicious packages for dYdX cryptocurrency exchange empties user wallets (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Incident is at least the third time the exchange has been targeted by thieves.

items.title: AI companies want you to stop chatting with bots and start managing them (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Claude Opus 4.6 and OpenAI Frontier pitch a future of supervising AI agents.

items.title: OpenAI is hoppin' mad about Anthropic's new Super Bowl TV ads (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Sam Altman calls AI competitor "dishonest" and "authoritarian" in lengthy post on X.

items.title: Increase of AI bots on the Internet sparks arms race (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Publishers are rolling out more aggressive defenses.

items.title: Microsoft releases urgent Office patch. Russian-state hackers pounce. (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: The window to patch vulnerabilities is shrinking rapidly.

items.title: Should AI chatbots have ads? Anthropic says no. (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: ChatGPT competitor comes out swinging with Super Bowl ad mocking AI product pitches.

items.title: So yeah, I vibe-coded a log colorizer-and I feel good about it (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Some semi-unhinged musings on where LLMs fit into my life-and how I'll keep using them.
